title: Arctiva — Linux, without the barriers.
description: Arctiva is an Arch Linux–based distribution with a graphical installer, KDE Plasma, automatic snapshots and gaming out of the box.
lead: A Linux distribution based on Arch Linux: the official Arch repositories and rolling releases, with a graphical installer, a familiar desktop and safe updates.
legal_independent: Arctiva is an independent project. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Arch Linux.
legal_license: The code is released under GPL-3.0-or-later. The name and the logo are not covered by that license: they are governed by the project's trademark policy.
roadmap_more: Full detail in the project's roadmap.
about_p: Arctiva is for people coming from Windows, or who want Arch without building it by hand. It keeps the best of Arch (unmodified official repositories, pacman and rolling releases) and adds what Arch lacks for everyday use: a graphical installer, a KDE Plasma desktop that feels familiar, simple updates with automatic snapshots to go back to, and games and graphics drivers without the fuss.

principles.p: Official core, extra and multilib, with no changes and no delay. If something in Arch breaks, we deal with it through warnings and snapshots instead of forking.
[arctiva] only holds Arctiva's own packages and is signed with GPG. The master key stays offline, and only the continuous integration system signs, never a personal computer.
The desktop is customised through settings and themes. KDE and Calamares are not modified, so Plasma updates don't get in the way.
Each ISO is pinned to a date of the Arch Linux Archive, so it can be rebuilt with exactly the same packages.
Arctiva will have its own help channels, so nobody gets sent to the Arch forums.
The code, design decisions and roadmap are public on GitHub.

feat.p: Try the full desktop without installing anything, then install with Calamares, with Basic, Gaming and Office profiles, optional disk encryption and an optional LTS kernel. Offline install: it copies the already-tested live system, so it is fast. UEFI only.

A KDE Plasma desktop in the style of Windows: taskbar at the bottom with centred icons, start menu with search, tray and clock. Light mode by default plus dark mode, the “Orbit” wallpaper and the Outfit typeface. A custom, always-visible boot menu (GRUB) theme, an animated boot screen (Plymouth) and a login screen with the Arctiva background.
Btrfs with Snapper: at most 10 are kept, and any of them can be booted from the GRUB menu.
Dolphin, high-refresh-rate displays (VRR), HDR; older X11 apps keep working through Xwayland.

Before touching the disk, a check warns you if Windows is hibernated or uses fast startup, or if BitLocker is on, and GRUB shows Windows automatically. Optional disk encryption asks for the password once.

AMD and Intel work out of the box. NVIDIA GTX 16 / RTX 20 and later are detected and get nvidia-open installed automatically. GTX 900/1000 cards use the free driver and the options are explained to you.
multilib on by default; Steam, Lutris, GameMode, MangoHud and Gamescope in the Gaming profile. Heroic Games Launcher and ProtonPlus are available as extras (Flatpak).
One native app with the pages Welcome, Personalisation, Updates, Applications, Drivers and Extras. Discover is gone: the store is the Center itself.

Search and install programs from the official Arch repositories and Flathub, with the source always visible and a recommended one. If updates are pending, it asks you to update first so the system isn't left half-updated. The AUR is available but off by default: turning it on shows a warning, you must read the PKGBUILD before every install, and its updates are manual and show what changed.

The “Windows programs” extra installs Bottles (Flatpak). When you open a .exe or .msi, a dedicated dialog explains what will happen, opens the file with Bottles and links to WineHQ AppDB, ProtonDB and Are We Anti-Cheat Yet?. Not everything works: games with anti-cheat, for example.

install_p: The graphical installer walks you through the whole process. Basic is always installed, with or without internet; extras are downloaded only when there is a connection.
snap_h: If an update fails, you go back
snap_p: Arctiva takes a snapshot before every update. If something fails, reboot, pick the previous snapshot in the GRUB menu and your system works again.

snap_lines.t: After the reboot, something is broken.

profiles.p: Plasma desktop, Firefox, snapshots and everything needed to start. Always installed.
Steam, Lutris, GameMode, MangoHud and Gamescope, with the 32-bit graphics libraries.
LibreOffice and Thunderbird in English, Spanish and Catalan, with spell checkers, compatible fonts, and scanner and printer support.

center_p: One app that brings Arctiva's tools together, with the look of Plasma.

center.p: Light, dark or automatic mode, accent colour, wallpaper, centred or left-aligned taskbar, floating taskbar, text size, screen scale and night light. Includes “Restore the Arctiva look” and “Advanced settings”.

Reads the archlinux.org news since your last update and blocks the update until you read any item that needs manual action. Flags delicate packages (kernel, NVIDIA, Mesa, systemd, Plasma), updates Flatpaks, and helps with .pacnew files.
The store: official Arch repositories and Flathub with the source always visible, and an optional AUR with warnings and a mandatory PKGBUILD read.
Shows the detected graphics card and what is missing, and installs it.
Games, Office, Windows programs (Bottles), Heroic Games Launcher, ProtonPlus, LTS kernel, printers and firewall: install and remove with a single switch.
Translates the usual failures ( conflicts, keys, disk space, no network ) into clear messages, without hiding the original text.
Admin actions go through a helper with a closed set of operations ( never arbitrary commands ) and ask for the password with the standard system dialog (polkit).
When GRUB is updated it is also reinstalled on the EFI partition, so your machine is never left unable to boot.

roadmap.t: Signed [arctiva] repository (not published yet) and graphics detection.
Store with Arch, Flathub and optional AUR; dialog for .exe and .msi.
GRUB theme, boot screen, login screen, Plasma theme and wallpapers.
0.8 first public beta published; hardware testing continues.

reqs: 25 GB of disk (40 GB recommended, because of snapshots)
USB drive of 4 GB or more
limits: Secure Boot is not supported in 1.0.
Hibernation won't be in 1.0; suspend works.
NVIDIA GTX 900/1000 cards use the free driver.
Some Windows programs and anti-cheat games may not work.
With disk encryption, GRUB asks for the password in text mode before loading the theme; that is normal.
beta_p: Arctiva 0.8.0 is the first public beta: expect rough edges and please report them. Download it from GitHub Releases and check it with the .sha256 and .sig files (key fingerprint above). The ISO weighs about 1.8 GiB. You can also build it from the source code.
community_p: Ask a question, follow the news or report a bug. It all happens on GitHub, and you need a free account to post.
support_p: Arctiva is free software. If you like it, you can help it keep going.
sp_gh_p: Sponsor Arctiva monthly or with a one-time contribution.
sp_coffee_h: No GitHub account? A coffee will do.
